title.narrative: Strengthen protective environment and empower women and girls in Yemen

description.narrative:
The project aims to contribute to the development of an enabling environment for gender equality, where there is zero tolerance for all forms of violence against women and children in public and private life; where women’s voice, agency, leadership and decision-making is strengthened in public, private and civic sphere; and lastly where women’s economic rights, empowerment and female entrepreneurship is promoted.
The project will strengthen the capacities of community-based organizations (CBOs) in 8 governorates in Yemen to enhance women’s rights, empowerment and gender equality. 18 CBOs will be supported to deliver prevention and support services for GBV survivors by running women community centers (WCC). In addition, INTERSOS will provide for trainings of local authorities and police.
Protection services will include the provision of individual case management (ICM), including psycho-social first aid (PSFA) and psychosocial counselling (PSC), referrals for specialized services (internally and externally) and follow-up. Referrals include e.g. psychological counseling, legal support, cash for protection (PCA), cash for health (CHA) and livelihoods. For each CBO, INTERSOS will provide minimum incentives for 2 social workers volunteers. Besides, INTERSOS will provide for small lumpsum for running costs of the local associations. Besides ICM, CBOs will also run collective PSS sessions, complementing ICM. CBOs will run awareness raising sessions on protection related topics for men, women, boys and girls. Awareness raising and collective PSS activities will be conducted at the WCCs.
Livelihood is one of the main components of the project, where CBOs will be supported to run livelihood courses, aimed at promoting women’s social-economic empowerment and female entrepreneurship

Main objective: Capacity building of CBOs/authorities/communities for community-based women protection prevention and response services for conflict affected communities in 8 governorates

description.narrative:
In November 2021, INTERSOS started the new phase of the project aiming to contribute to the development of an enabling environment for gender equality, where there is zero tolerance for all forms of violence against women and children in public and private life; where women’s voice, agency, leadership, and decision-making is strengthened in public, private and civic sphere; and lastly where women’s economic rights, empowerment and female entrepreneurship is promoted. The project continues to strengthen the capacities of community-based organizations (18 CBOs) in 8 governorates in Yemen, 4 in South and 4 in North Yemen, to enhance women’s rights, empowerment, and gender equality. • South: Aden, Lahj, Hadramout (Hadramout Al-Sahel and Wadi Hadramout). • North: Sana’a, Amana Al-Asima, Ibb and Hajja.
The project aims to strengthen prevention and response to women's protection issues and to empower women and girls socially-economically in Yemen by the following: • Capacity building for CBOs and Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (MOSAL). • Training for police officers and local authorities on women protection. • Community awareness sessions for the community at large (men and women), community leaders (focus on men), and for youth (separate sessions for girls and boys). • Monitor and audit case management services provided by local CBOs. • Provide cash for protection to women protection cases (direct financial support for legal, safe shelter, etc.). • Provide cash for health assistance to acute/emergency cases. • Provide collective PSS sessions for local community members. • Organize informal skills trainings (IDP, returnees, and host community) for women and girls to enhance their self-reliance and reduce vulnerability

title.narrative: Result 1: Capacity building of CBOs/authorities/communities for community-based women protection prevention and response services for conflict affected communities in 8 governorates
Indicator 1.3: 10,800 persons (25% male and 75% female) participate in community awareness sessions and increase their awareness about women protection prevention and response
Indicator 1.1: 50 staff/volunteers of local CBOs (44) and MoSAL (6) gain improved skills and knowledge in women protection case management (80% women and 20% men).

Indicator 1.2: 180 police officers and local authorities (30 police officer and 15 authority officials per 4 governorates in the South) (min 25% women) annually gained improved skills and knowledge in women protection.
Result 3: Women’s economic rights and empowerment strengthened and female entrepreneurship for women protection cases encouraged
Indicator 3.1: 2,160 women and girls (women protection cases) participate in informal skills trainings (IDP and host community)
Indicator 3.2: Minimum 10% of beneficiaries in the informal skills training are women or girls with disabilities.
Indicator 3.3: Minimum 80% of beneficiaries in informal skills training report to have adopted positive coping mechanism following the courses and kits distribution
Result 2: Availability of local quality services for women protection cases is assured by supporting local associations in service delivery
Indicator 2.6: % of women beneficiaries (20-24 yrs) accessing INTERSOS/local partners’ services were married or in union before ages 15 and 18
